data.hypothesis: A dynamic pixel schedule with chunks of 64 should balance spatially varying hit and ambient-occlusion work better than a static contiguous partition while keeping scheduling overhead bounded. Per-pixel SplitMix64 streams seeded from one serial draw should make samples independent of worker scheduling and thread count; the one-worker path avoids OpenMP overhead.
data.notes: The supplied build diagnostic confirms RenderInput has no seed field, so each render obtains its root seed from the caller-seeded drand48 state once before any OpenMP workers start. Each pixel then uses only its local PRNG state. No candidate correctness or timing measurements are available yet; the controller should evaluate all official configurations and repeated timings.
transformations: Initialize one render seed serially from the caller's drand48 state, then derive independent per-pixel SplitMix64 streams.
Parallelize flattened pixel iterations with OpenMP dynamic scheduling in 64-pixel chunks and request no more than the supplied worker count.
Keep a direct serial loop for the one-worker case and preserve the primary sample and ambient-ray loop counts.
